newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS STABLE ON HOLIDAY EVE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS STABLE ON HOLIDAY EVE.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed Friday stable against the U.S. dollar in little-to-no trade ahead of a long weekend holiday.
But foreign currency movements on the world market left the Zimbabwe unit softer against the German mark and firmer to pound sterling and the rand of neighbouring South Africa.

"Very little happened here...and the movements we saw reflected activity on the international market. I think it's fair to say we will start the way we ended -- in a holiday mood," one dealer said of Monday and Tuesday, public and market Heroes' and Defence Forces holidays.
"We should expect (local) trade to be squeezed and the (Zimbabwe) dollar to just respond to external factors," he added.

The Zimbabwe dollar ended Friday at its overnight level of 11.6350/6450 to the U.S. dollar, but it closed firmer to pound sterling at 18.3200/3700 from Thursday's 18.4000/4500 and its Friday morning rating of 18.5000/5500.

Against the mark it ended the day weaker at 6.2500/2600 from a morning rating of 6.2200/2300 and 6.1995/2180 overnight but the local unit gained slightly on the rand, closing at 2.4800/4900 from 2.4900/5000 when the market opened on Friday, and from 2.4805/4850 at its Thursday close.
